---
title: "NatuRA"
subtitle: "Sustainable use of mountain grasslands"
---

NatuRA studies the sustainable use of natural resources in alpine and mountain grassland ecosystems under global change. I am the project leader. The project runs from March 2025 to February 2028 and is a collaboration between institutions in Norway and South Africa, funded by the Research Council of Norway and the National Research Foundation of South Africa.

Mountain grasslands provide grazing for wildlife and livestock, clean water, carbon storage, and support for traditional ways of life. In many mountain regions they have been managed as communal rangelands, and pastoralism has been central to that management. Those ecosystems, and the communities that depend on them, are now under pressure from environmental and social change.

The traditional management of these grasslands, including grazing and water use, is similar across mountain regions that are otherwise far apart. NatuRA uses that shared basis to compare strategies and to develop nature-based solutions with local communities. The aim is to keep the ecosystems, and the livelihoods they support, resilient.

The project is led by the University of Bergen and the Universities of the Free State and Venda. Partners include the University of Pretoria, Meat Naturally, Witsieshoek Mountain Lodge, and the Bakoena Royal Council in South Africa, and the Heathland Centre and Sogn Jord- og Hagebruksskule in Norway.

The public project description is on the [University of Bergen project page](https://www4.uib.no/en/research/research-projects/natura).
